events.description: Sudan's NIF, Iran and Bin Ladin were said to share common anti-imperialist objectives. They agreed to collaborate politically and militarily, primarily against Israel and the US and secondarily against Arab regimes that supported them.
CIA information report on the establishment of the tripartite agreement was disseminated.
Circa 1991, the NIF and Iran were said to share anti-imperialist objectives and to need to coordinate. The idea of a tripartite front of Shia and Sunni Islamists was floated.

An agreement was reached among bin Ladin, Iran and the NIF to collaborate politically and militarily. The primary goal was to confront Israel and the US, and the secondary goal was to undermine Arab regimes supporting them.
CIA information report disseminated (TOT 311834Z JAN 97) on the establishment of the tripartite agreement.

sources_cited: CIA information report, 31 January 1997 (not finally evaluated intelligence)
key_claims: Circa 1991, the Sudanese NIF, Iran and Usama bin Ladin were said to have formed a tripartite agreement to collaborate politically and militarily.
The primary goal was to confront Israel and the United States, and the secondary goal was to undermine Arab regimes supporting them.
Shia and Sunni Islamists might effectively coordinate against common enemies through a tripartite front.
Hizballah and Iranian expertise was to be transferred to extremist groups, including Islamic Army members.
